Complete case study: harbour seal scat DNA metabarcoding (Salish Sea)

Source: vignettes/articles/case-study-dna-seals.Rmd
case-study-dna-seals.Rmd

Question, source and sampling unit

Research question. Which prey groups are detected in harbour seal scats, how does their relative DNA signal vary among groups of samples, and how much taxonomic information is lost at finer ranks? This is a descriptive worked analysis; it does not estimate ingested biomass or prove a difference between seasons or laboratories.

We use the real, packaged salish_seal_dna data of Thomas et al. (2022): 4,625 harbour seal (Phoca vitulina) scats from 52 Salish Sea haul-outs, 2012–2018. Each row is a prey assignment within one scat. This is a secondary analysis of the published taxon-level dataset, not a rerun of the raw-sequence pipeline. The released diet_fraction is an already calculated within-scat DNA fraction, combining information from 16S and COI markers. The frozen WoRMS taxonomy, salish_seal_lineage, avoids live API lookups. The data source and CC0 status are documented in ?salish_seal_dna.

Unit: one sample_id (scat). Taxon key: prey_label. Quantity: diet_fraction, not prey grams. Covariates: site, year, season and lab.

library(DietView)
dat <- salish_seal_dna
lin <- salish_seal_lineage
c(records = nrow(dat), scats = length(unique(dat$sample_id)),
  prey_labels = length(unique(dat$prey_label)), sites = length(unique(dat$site)))
#>     records       scats prey_labels       sites 
#>       11641        4625         117          52
head(dat[, c("sample_id", "prey_label", "diet_fraction", "season", "lab")])
#>   sample_id             prey_label diet_fraction season lab
#> 1  Pv12.001      Alosa sapidissima        0.9731 spring UBC
#> 2  Pv12.001        Clupea pallasii        0.0163 spring UBC
#> 3  Pv12.001  Metacarcinus magister        0.0106 spring UBC
#> 4  Pv12.002        Clupea pallasii        0.2859 spring UBC
#> 5  Pv12.002 Gasterosteus aculeatus        0.7141 spring UBC
#> 6  Pv12.003      Alosa sapidissima        0.0385 spring UBC

Audit the input before analysis

A fraction should be finite, non-negative and, in these released data, sum to approximately one within each positive scat. These checks are diagnostic: they should not be used to silently remove unexpected values.

stopifnot(!anyNA(dat$sample_id), !anyNA(dat$prey_label))
stopifnot(all(is.finite(dat$diet_fraction)), all(dat$diet_fraction >= 0))
scat_total <- tapply(dat$diet_fraction, dat$sample_id, sum)
summary(scat_total)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>  0.9994  1.0000  1.0000  1.0000  1.0000  1.0005
max(abs(scat_total - 1))
#> [1] 6e-04
frame <- unique(dat[, c("sample_id", "site", "year", "season", "lab")])
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(frame$sample_id))
print(table(frame$season, useNA = "ifany"))
#> 
#> winter spring summer autumn 
#>    288   1603   1622   1112
print(table(frame$lab, useNA = "ifany"))
#> 
#>  DFO  UBC WDFW 
#> 1173 1484 1968

Interpretation. frame counts scats, not prey records. Samples can contain several prey detections. Without a complete list of all scats processed we cannot calculate a survey-wide negative-detection or extraction-failure rate: these released rows describe the samples represented in the published table.

Specify roles and freeze the taxonomy

weight_type = "rra" asks DietView to normalize the quantity within each sample. Here the original fractions are already normalized; applying this operation again is effectively idempotent (apart from numeric rounding). For raw ASV read counts, the same argument first performs the normalization; see the separate ASV case study.

spec <- dv_spec(
  predator = "predator", stomach = "sample_id", prey_name = "prey_label",
  weight = "diet_fraction", weight_type = "rra", unit_label = "scat",
  covariates = c("site", "year", "season", "lab")
)
prep <- dv_prepare(dat, spec, taxonomy = "table", lineage = lin,
                   verbose = FALSE)
prep
#> <dietview_prep>
#>   records   : 11641 
#>   scats     : 4625 
#>   predators : 1 
#>   ranks     : kingdom > phylum > class > order > family > genus > species 
#>   covariates: site, year, season, lab 
#>   source    : table
c(raw_quantity = "diet_fraction", normalized_column = prep$spec$weight)
#>      raw_quantity normalized_column 
#>   "diet_fraction"             "rra"
normalized <- tapply(prep$data[[prep$spec$weight]], prep$data$sample_id, sum)
summary(normalized)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>       1       1       1       1       1       1
stopifnot(all(abs(normalized[scat_total > 0] - 1) < 1e-6))

The frozen classification retains the shared ranks for ambiguous assignments such as two alternative rockfish species, instead of choosing one arbitrarily. A prey label with more than one candidate is not a precise species identification.

head(lin[lin$n_candidates > 1,
         c("prey_label", "family", "genus", "species", "n_candidates")])
#>                                                      prey_label         family
#> 11                   Artedius fenestralis OR Artedius lateralis       Cottidae
#> 13                  Artedius lateralis OR Artedius notospilotus       Cottidae
#> 54              Lepidopsetta bilineata OR Platichthys stellatus Pleuronectidae
#> 102           Scorpaenichthys marmoratus OR Leptocottus armatus           <NA>
#> 104 Sebastes caurinus OR Sebastes maliger OR Sebastes nebulosus     Sebastidae
#> 106                      Sebastes flavidus OR Sebastes melanops     Sebastidae
#>        genus species n_candidates
#> 11  Artedius    <NA>            2
#> 13  Artedius    <NA>            2
#> 54      <NA>    <NA>            2
#> 102     <NA>    <NA>            2
#> 104 Sebastes    <NA>            3
#> 106 Sebastes    <NA>            2

Describe the sample before the diet 

dv_summary(prep, by = "season")
#>       predator season n_stomachs n_records n_taxa records_per_stomach
#> 1 Harbour seal summer       1622      4379     97                2.70
#> 2 Harbour seal spring       1603      3787     90                2.36
#> 3 Harbour seal autumn       1112      2643     74                2.38
#> 4 Harbour seal winter        288       832     66                2.89
#>   total_weight
#> 1         1622
#> 2         1603
#> 3         1112
#> 4          288

The numbers describe this collection of scats, not a random sample of all seal feeding in the Salish Sea. Seasonal contrasts are confounded by site, year, laboratory and collection effort unless the design is addressed.

Calculate three different measures

The three columns below measure different things. pct_occ is the share of taxon–scat records; it is not frequency of occurrence. pct_w is the sample-normalized relative DNA read signal. pct_fo is the proportion of represented scats in which a taxon was detected, at the requested rank.

tree <- dv_tree(prep)
family <- dv_rank_table(tree, "Family")
head(family[order(-family$pct_w),
            c("label", "value_occ", "pct_occ", "pct_w")], 10)
#>             label value_occ   pct_occ     pct_w
#> 52   Merlucciidae      1755 15.076024 23.549770
#> 49      Clupeidae      1948 16.733958 22.119605
#> 84     Salmonidae      2308 19.826475 16.157408
#> 59   Embiotocidae       611  5.248690  5.437847
#> 64       Cottidae       756  6.494287  5.068601
#> 51        Gadidae       871  7.482175  4.935487
#> 46 Batrachoididae       608  5.222919  4.779365
#> 83 Pleuronectidae       598  5.137016  3.532447
#> 50    Engraulidae       233  2.001546  2.737961
#> 48       Alosidae       229  1.967185  1.914067
fo <- dv_fo_table(prep, rank = "family", denominator = "nonempty")
head(fo[order(-fo$pct_fo), c("taxon", "n_stomachs", "n_total", "pct_fo")], 10)
#>             taxon n_stomachs n_total pct_fo
#> 1       Clupeidae       1948    4625  42.12
#> 2    Merlucciidae       1755    4625  37.95
#> 3      Salmonidae       1309    4625  28.30
#> 4         Gadidae        803    4625  17.36
#> 5        Cottidae        610    4625  13.19
#> 6  Batrachoididae        608    4625  13.15
#> 7    Embiotocidae        595    4625  12.86
#> 8  Pleuronectidae        420    4625   9.08
#> 9     Engraulidae        233    4625   5.04
#> 10       Alosidae        229    4625   4.95

At each taxonomic rank, DietView retains an unidentified category. A family label NA may occur beneath different parent taxa; use the hierarchy when reading such cells rather than combining their labels indiscriminately.

ranks <- unique(as.character(tree$rank))
totals <- vapply(ranks, function(r) {
  x <- tree[tree$rank == r, ]
  sum(x$pct_w)
}, numeric(1))
round(totals, 6)
#> Kingdom  Phylum   Class   Order  Family   Genus Species 
#>     100     100     100     100     100     100     100
stopifnot(all(abs(totals - 100) < 1e-4))

Render and interpret a real interactive figure 

dv_sunburst(tree, mode = "weight",
            title = "Harbour seal scats — within-scat relative DNA signal",
            subtitle = "Mean RRA, not prey biomass")

Read the rings from coarse to fine. Each ring partitions the same normalized DNA signal, with white segments for material not identified below a particular rank. A large wedge says more DNA signal in these samples, not necessarily more prey individuals, biomass or energy. Marker efficiency, primer bias, digestion, reference-library coverage and laboratory methods all matter.

Identification resolution and stratification 

res <- dv_resolution(prep, by = "lab")
head(res[, c("lab", "finest_rank", "n_records", "p_records", "p_weight")], 12)

As a descriptive comparison, prepare two sample-level strata from the frozen data. Do not interpret unadjusted contrasts as ecological trends.

season_sizes <- sort(table(frame$season), decreasing = TRUE)
season_sizes
#> 
#> summer spring autumn winter 
#>   1622   1603   1112    288
major <- names(season_sizes)[seq_len(min(2L, length(season_sizes)))]
season_tables <- lapply(major, function(s) {
  ds <- dat[!is.na(dat$season) & as.character(dat$season) == s, ]
  ps <- dv_prepare(ds, spec, taxonomy = "table", lineage = lin,
                   verbose = FALSE)
  tb <- dv_rank_table(dv_tree(ps), "Family")
  data.frame(season = s, tb[, c("label", "pct_w")])
})
head(do.call(rbind, season_tables), 12)
#>    season           label      pct_w
#> 73 summer      Salmonidae 13.1572756
#> 47 summer    Merlucciidae 29.2026101
#> 44 summer       Clupeidae 22.1525452
#> 46 summer         Gadidae  4.9911108
#> 72 summer  Pleuronectidae  3.7357248
#> 55 summer        Cottidae  3.3701229
#> 42 summer  Batrachoididae  3.9386076
#> 51 summer    Embiotocidae  3.5979804
#> 45 summer     Engraulidae  3.3211028
#> 57 summer  Gasterosteidae  0.8380219
#> 43 summer        Alosidae  1.4002699
#> 40 summer Petromyzontidae  0.4822053

Export data and prepare a dashboard

dv_matrix() produces a scat-by-taxon numeric matrix for downstream analysis; rows are scats, not repeated prey records. The weight currency contains sample-normalized proportions here.

m <- dv_matrix(prep, rank = "family", currency = "weight")
c(samples = nrow(m), families_and_unidentified = ncol(m))
#>                   samples families_and_unidentified 
#>                      4625                        57
head(round(rowSums(m), 5))
#> PG001 PG002 PG005 PG006 PG007 PG010 
#>     1     1     1     1     1     1
export <- file.path(tempdir(), "salish_seal_family_rra.csv")
utils::write.csv(m, export, row.names = TRUE)
file.exists(export)
#> [1] TRUE

Build a single-file HTML dashboard on your own computer. This optional step is not run while the vignette is built, since it writes a second large HTML file; run it interactively when you want to share the result.

dv_build_html(prep,
  output = file.path(getwd(), "salish_seal_dna_dashboard.html"),
  bands = c("occurrence", "weight"), strata = c("season", "lab"),
  min_stomachs = 25,
  title = "Harbour seal DNA diet — Salish Sea (descriptive)")

What to report, and what not to infer

Report the source, license, date, marker and laboratory, sampling unit, preprocessing, unique sample count per stratum, treatment of ambiguous taxa, classification version, metric/denominator, and exclusions. In a scientific study, add sampling-design-aware uncertainty intervals and evaluate batch, site and year effects. Do not equate DNA reads or RRA to biomass or individual consumption; a detection in a scat is not proof of a particular meal size. This vignette describes detection patterns, not causal or population-level seasonal changes.

References: Thomas et al. (2022), Scientific Data 9:68, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-022-01152-5 (data CC0); Deagle et al. (2019), Molecular Ecology 28:391–406, https://doi.org/10.1111/mec.14734.
